gh-issue.description: GitHub issue: desc, comments, images, linked PRs. :full = no truncation, all comments. Targets another repo with a leading repo:OWNER/NAME op.

gh-issues.description: Issue triage board: list issues (no default author filter — the queue, not mine), ranked unrankable → external author → stale body → no linked PR → oldest. Per issue: linked-PR state from the timeline, external-filer marker from GitHub's authorAssociation, age, comment count, labels, stale-body flag (newest comment newer than lastEditedAt, or createdAt when the body was never edited), and the milestone as '[m:TITLE]' — no column, so a row without one costs nothing and '[m:?]' means gh did not answer rather than 'none'. Enrichment is one GraphQL call per 20 issues; when it fails the derived fields render '?' and the footer names why — never 0, never 'internal', never 'no PR'. An unrecognised token or filter key is REFUSED, never dropped: an unnarrowed board printed for a filter nobody applied reads as the answer to the question you asked. Filters (comma-sep): author/assignee/label/milestone/state/per. Flags: nopipe (skip enrichment), iids, external, stale, nomilestone (client-side, so it declines outright if any row's milestone is unknown; the --limit disclosure is measured against the fetch, not against what survived the filter).

gh-issue-create.description: Create a GitHub issue from a JSON/TOML payload file. Supports labels, assignees, and milestone (by title).

gh-pr-create.description: Open a pull request from a JSON/TOML payload file, and hand back the receipt the four hand-rolled calls used to assemble. Payload route because a PR body is long markdown with colons and fences that cannot survive :-tokenization. base is REQUIRED and is never defaulted — master and a release branch are equally plausible from one cwd, and a wrong base silently retargets the merge; head defaults to the current branch and repo to the origin remote, both stated with their source so a wrong one is visible immediately. The receipt names: number and URL; base/head as resolved; whether any check actually STARTED (zero checks is rendered as 'nothing has been created', never as pending, with the ~15min creation window and a stated UNKNOWN past it); the issues the body links, parsed with the same closing-reference reader gh-pr uses, so a malformed Closes line is caught at creation rather than after the merge; and the next command. Ends on a one-line [result] verdict.

gh-pr-merge.description: Merge a PR and PROVE it landed — the only op in this family that writes. Refuses first: not OPEN, draft, CONFLICTING, mergeable=UNKNOWN, mergeStateStatus not CLEAN, CHANGES_REQUESTED, zero check runs, an unreadable rollup, any leg that is not a pass (#454's arithmetic — cancelled/skipped/timed_out/neutral/action_required are each named and none is permission), and a leg tally that could not be reconciled against what the runs declare (a doubt is not permission on a gate, the same call gh-branch's verdict makes). There is no green-bypass; a refusal names the manual command instead. Without |force it previews the gate and merges nothing (_publish_safety.require_confirm, same gate as the publish ops). After merging it reads state/mergedAt/mergeCommit back off the remote — a zero exit is not a merge — then checks EVERY linked issue individually, reconciling the body's own closing refs against GitHub's closingIssuesReferences so a ref GitHub never bound is named (PR #908's shape: body said Closes #899, GitHub bound nothing, no error anywhere), each unclosed one carrying the exact command to close it by hand. Then reports the DEFAULT BRANCH's state after the squash via gh-branch, because a green PR is a statement about its merge-base. Names the head branch and worktree cleanup command but never runs it. Exits 0 only when the merge is verified AND every linked issue is verified closed; a merged-but-issue-open partial is never rendered as a success and never implies a rollback.

gh-pr.description: Review a pull request: branch, checks, reviews/approval, linked issue, diff stat, comments — the full dashboard. A truncated description says so twice — in the header and at the cut — with the exact char count withheld; :full uncaps it. :status = slim merge-state only (~250B, fits hook cache). :diff is the merge gate's own read, in the shape a reviewer walks rather than the whole patch: the file list with per-file +/-, heaviest first, with '[same edit xN]' noting a file whose every hunk is the identical change — a note, never a filter. :diff:PATH is that one file's hunks, fenced. A diff that could not be fetched says so and exits 1 instead of rendering an empty file list; a PATH not in the diff declines and names the paths that are; both caps (GH_PR_DIFF_MAX_FILES, default 60; GH_PR_DIFF_MAX_BYTES, default 65536) disclose exactly what they withheld. Honours repo:OWNER/NAME, which raw `gh pr diff` from the wrong directory does not.

gh-prs.description: PR triage board: list PRs (default author=@me), sorted failing-first. Per PR: check rollup (failed→check name), approval (reviewDecision), age, diff size, watch-state, draft/conflict/threads flags + actionable footer. Filters (comma-sep): author/reviewer/assignee/label/state/per. Flags: nopipe (skip review-thread enrichment), iids, failed. A token outside those two lists, or a state outside open/closed/merged/all, is REFUSED (exit 1, no board) rather than dropped. The core board is one gh call; review threads enrich in parallel.

gh-run.description: What passed, what failed? Workflow run jobs with statuses and failed step names. Targets another repo with a leading repo:OWNER/NAME op.

gh-branch.description: Is this branch green? Answers for a *branch* — the shape gh-pr cannot take, because after a squash merge the ref that matters is the default branch and it has no PR. Selects runs by workflow identity, never by recency: `gh run list --limit 1` returns whichever workflow started last (routinely CodeQL) and reports its conclusion for the commit, which is how a green gets read off a run that is not the run you meant. The summary is conjunctive — green only when EVERY workflow on the head SHA concluded and every leg passed — and it states four things apart that collapse into each other by default: GREEN, NOT GREEN (failed, or not finished — worded differently), NO RUN (nothing exists for this SHA, with the reason and the ~15min creation window), and UNKNOWN (a job list did not come back — never counted as zero passing legs). Leg counts come from the same _checks.summarize tally as gh-pr/gh-run, so `2 cancelled` is named rather than dropped and the terms sum to the leg count. Names the head SHA, because green is a claim about a commit. Every row says `concluded` or `running` in words, so no bare column can be misread as a leg state. With no argument, answers for the repo default branch — the shape used right after a merge. Exit 0 only when GREEN. Targets another repo with a leading repo:OWNER/NAME op.

gh-job.description: Why did this job fail? PR context + error pattern search + log tail. Takes EITHER id namespace: a check-run id (CodeQL, Dependabot, external CI) renders the check run — status, output, annotations — under '# Check run #N' with a 'Routed:' line naming the switch, so you never have to know which of GitHub's two lists a red leg landed in; the checks API is only consulted after the Actions endpoint 404s, so working calls cost nothing extra, and a checks call that does not answer declines rather than rendering an empty check. :fail (alias :errors) = matched failure blocks only, no tail — the tight triage view, per-job patterns; :raw dumps full trace; :raw:START[:END] slices lines (1-indexed, inclusive); :raw:-N is the last N lines; a START past the end returns the tail of the width requested and says so rather than declining; :grep:PATTERN ad-hoc regex over the log (literal fallback, context, tail on no-match; emission budgeted by GH_JOB_GREP_MAX_BYTES, default 65536 — a capped view says so in its header AND footer with an exact 'N of M matching lines shown' and names bytes, not a match limit, as what cut)

gh-check.description: What did this check run say? The *other* id namespace: CodeQL, Dependabot, code-scanning uploads and external CI report through the checks API, not through Actions, so gh-job 404s on their ids. gh-check:ID prints the check run's status, output title/summary and its annotations — path:line, title, message, which for a scanning check is the whole finding — capped at GH_CHECK_ANNOTATION_CAP (default 5) with a '+N more' disclosure in header AND footer. Zero annotations on a non-passing check is never rendered as an all-clear, and a failed annotations fetch is never rendered as zero. gh-check:pr:N lists the check runs on PR N's head commit with their ids, because gh-pr:N:status names a non-Actions leg without one. A 404 probes the Actions namespace and, when the id is a job, says so and names gh-job. Since #827 this is the explicit form rather than the only route — gh-job:ID answers for a check run too, and gh-pr names a non-Actions leg as 'CodeQL (check #ID)'. Does not read the code-scanning API.

gh-follow.description: Follow a GitHub user via the authenticated gh CLI session.

gh-following.description: List users you follow on GitHub.

gh-batch-follow.description: Follow each username from a file (one per line, '#' comments). Sleeps 1s between calls.

gh-star.description: Star a GitHub repository via gh CLI.

gh-batch-star.description: Star each OWNER/REPO from a file (one per line, '#' comments). Sleeps 1s between calls.

gh-find-followable.description: Discover candidate users to follow: pulls stargazers + contributors of a repo, dedupes, filters out orgs. Pipe to a file then review before gh-batch-follow.

gh-find-starable.description: Discover repos worth starring by topic. Pulls top N repos for the topic, sorted by stars. Pipe to a file then review before gh-batch-star.
